key_headlines.title: Korea Posts OECD-Leading Q1 GDP Growth as Deputy Minister Promotes Investment in Paris
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Minister Huh Jang held a Korean economic briefing for global investors in Paris, highlighting Korea's top-tier OECD growth rate, strong exports, and current account surplus. The government is also advancing plans for 24-hour market operations and an offshore won settlement system.

key_headlines.title: Government Fast-Tracks Jangseong Data Center Project in Jeollanam-do
key_headlines.summary: The government is accelerating the construction of an advanced data center in Jangseong County, Jeollanam-do by exempting local finance investment reviews. The project aims for completion by 2027 and operational launch by 2028.

key_headlines.title: Won Weakens Despite 36 Consecutive Months of Current Account Surplus
key_headlines.summary: Korea's currency has fallen to its weakest level since the 2009 global financial crisis despite maintaining a 36-month consecutive current account surplus of 43 trillion won, dampening domestic consumption.

key_headlines.title: Deputy Minister Highlights Korea Equities' Shift to 'Korea Premium' Premium Amid Capital Market Reforms
key_headlines.summary: Huh Jang emphasized Korea's market reforms including corporate law amendments and enhanced shareholder returns, noting 18.7 billion dollars in net foreign inflows to Korean government bonds following WGBI inclusion.

key_headlines.title: Google Signs 46.8 Trillion Won AI Data Center Cloud Rental Contract with SpaceX
key_headlines.summary: Google agreed to a long-term deal with SpaceX to rent high-performance computing resources for 920 million dollars monthly from October 2026 to June 2029, reflecting intense competition among tech giants for AI infrastructure.

sections.Hot Economy News: Korea's first-quarter GDP growth rate leads OECD economies, and the government is actively promoting investment through international briefings highlighting strong semiconductor exports and current account surpluses. A major data center project in Jeollanam-do is being fast-tracked for development, while significant infrastructure investments are underway to support AI and digital transformation. However, the won currency continues to weaken despite favorable macroeconomic fundamentals, creating headwinds for domestic consumption and household sentiment.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Korea's fiscal deficit is widening amid youth employment rates declining for 24 consecutive months, though the government maintains its budget position remains sound relative to major economies due to rapid GDP growth from semiconductor strength. The OECD forecasts Korea's potential growth rate will fall below 1.5% for the first time next year, highlighting structural economic limitations despite current export momentum. U.S. inflation data and Federal Reserve policy decisions remain critical variables affecting global economic outlook, with CPI and PPI releases scheduled for this week ahead of the FOMC meeting.
sections.Financial Markets: U.S. Treasury yields have surged to levels not seen in years, with two-year yields reaching 16-month highs amid inflation concerns, particularly following geopolitical tensions in Iran. The S&P 500 index plummeted 5.54% last Friday, triggering a broad market decline affecting stocks, bonds, and cryptocurrencies simultaneously as investors fear potential interest rate hikes. Korean markets face significant headwinds from U.S. rate pressures, with Kospi futures down 8% as foreign investor participation continues to decline. The upcoming FOMC meeting under new Fed Chair Kevin Wash carries heightened significance, with markets pricing in a 60% probability of year-end rate increases despite political pressure for rate cuts.
sections.Industry & Technology: The semiconductor sector benefits from won depreciation and strong export demand, while battery makers including LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK Innovation face pressures from rising raw material costs and foreign exchange losses. LFP batteries, increasingly dominant in the electric vehicle market, lack economic recycling viability, prompting government consideration of recycling mandate policies. Korea's nuclear export business to Czech Republic is accelerating following resolution of EU subsidy concerns, with opportunities for robot and battery industry cooperation. Ferrari's first pure electric vehicle, the Luce, faces market skepticism despite premium positioning, illustrating the challenges luxury brands face in electric vehicle transition.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's reconstruction and redevelopment projects significantly influence housing market sentiment, with areas like Apgujeong showing 85% support and Yeouido 72% support for these initiatives in recent elections. June apartment supply surges to 40,000 units, with 22,059 units concentrated in Seoul metropolitan area, representing a fourfold increase from the same period last year. Rental housing shortages intensify as reconstruction projects create supply constraints, with Seoul apartment rental listings declining to 33,244 units compared to year-ago levels. Dongtan in Gyeonggi Province posts the nation's highest apartment price appreciation rate, triggering renewed concerns about balloon effects and potential government land transaction restrictions.
sections.International Economy: The upcoming Federal Reserve meeting under new Chair Kevin Wash has become a critical focal point for global markets, with President Trump advocating for rate cuts despite strong employment data. New Fed Chair Wash faces pressure from both inflation concerns and political demands to lower rates, with market expectations divided on the central bank's next move. SpaceX's successful Starship V3 test flight and Google's massive AI data center contract demonstrate escalating competition for computing infrastructure among tech giants, with implications for U.S. technology leadership. U.S. CPI and PPI data releases this week are expected to show inflation pressures, potentially influencing the Fed's forward guidance and global market stability.
sections.AI & Economy: Google signed a landmark 46.8 trillion won contract with SpaceX to rent AI data center computing resources through June 2029, reflecting intensifying competition for computing infrastructure among technology giants. SpaceX's successful Starship V3 test flight raises prospects for space-based data centers as demand from generative AI proliferation drives unprecedented computing infrastructure needs. Employment Minister Kim Young-hoon is attending the International Labour Organization summit to discuss human-centered AI transformation and labor market changes with major nations. Financial regulators are exploring expanded application of model risk management frameworks to AI systems as the technology's use accelerates across the financial sector.
sections.Others: The 2026 FIFA World Cup in North America will feature 48 participating nations and expanded matches, generating approximately 6.5 billion dollars in broadcast rights and sponsorship revenue. U.S. Section 301 investigation into forced labor production includes Korea alongside 59 other economies, signaling new trade pressure mechanisms beyond traditional human rights enforcement. Major tech companies including Google, Microsoft, and Meta are increasingly relying on external financing for AI infrastructure investments, with semiconductor suppliers and backend manufacturers capturing significant economic value. The government accelerates African Swine Fever vaccine development and commercialization by opening quarantine headquarters' specialized research facilities to private sector partners.
